description: Pre-solve gate for hull-surface geometry and volume-mesh quality used by the ship overall-performance solvers. All thresholds are data; the engine (backend/services/geometry_validation) contains none of them.

skin_friction_correlation.citation: Schlichting (1979) Boundary-Layer Theory: local skin-friction power law cf = 0.0576 Re^-0.2 for a turbulent flat plate, 5e5 < Re < 1e7

envelopes.citation: Geometric identity: for any body inside its own bounding box, Cb = volume/(L*B*T) <= 1 and Cwp = Aw/(L*B) <= 1. There is deliberately no lower bound on Cwp: a fine hull whose maximum beam lies below the design waterline is legitimately ~0 there.
envelopes.description: Archimedes / bounding-box identity — values outside these bounds are geometrically impossible, not merely extrapolated.

envelopes.citation: Holtrop & Mennen (1982), An approximate power prediction method, International Shipbuilding Progress 29(335): validity 0.55 <= Cb <= 0.85, 3.9 <= L/B <= 14.9, 2.1 <= B/T <= 4.0
envelopes.description: Applicability range of the Holtrop-Mennen resistance/power regression; outside it the empirical prediction is an extrapolation and must be flagged.

envelopes.citation: ITTC-1978 performance prediction procedure / Michell slender-body regime as tabulated for fine hulls: 0.35 <= Cb <= 0.65 with L/B >= 6.0 and B/T <= 5.0
envelopes.description: Fine-form (slender-body) regime; hulls outside it should not be evaluated with wave-resistance slender-body theory.
